text:
Maria: Heads up: observed slow steady GPU resident growth on a couple dedicated nodes after ~12h of throughput. Memory not dropping between chat sessions.
Maria: I attached a short nvprof and a pytorch trace, small repro in the message below.
Maria: Sure. Minimal loop hitting KV-heavy chat history (ctx 8k):
```
FOR i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long history..."}] }'; \
  sleep 0.2; \
done
```
Maria: ran with REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_MAX=512M, REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=on
Kevin: did you try pinning kernels (force selector) to rule out kernel flips creating new workspace shapes?
Maria: yes. REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=baseline reduced slope but growth still present. REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=tiled gave a larger initial bump but then slower drift.
Diana: could be fragmentation vs real leak. Try focused evict/restore to pressure freelist (writes then explicit evict every N).
Maria: added repro_kv_eviction.py --evict-every 10 --requests 20000. tail shows resident: 12.1G -> 13.3G -> 13.7G.
infra-bot: CI job queued: eng-runtime/gpu-mem-repro#789 (will run with ASAN/jemalloc configs).
Kevin: enable DEBUG_ALLOC=1, export MALLOC_CONF='oversize_threshold:0, background_thread:true' or appropriate jemalloc opts, and capture bins.
Maria: jemalloc dump attached: top increasing arenas: 64k, 256k, 1M buckets 20h into run.
Diana: that pattern screams mid-size fragmentation. Are KV items pinned preventing coalescing? eviction policy may leave many mid-size holes.
Kevin: another angle: batching spikes create occasional huge workspace requests. If kernel family alternates (tile vs baseline) allocator may split slabs to satisfy incompatible alignment/size and never fully reuse.
Maria: confirmed: forcing REDWOOD_KERNEL_ROUTE=static + KV_LIMIT=1G stabilizes memory for 24h in the repro. Reverting KV_LIMIT reintroduces drift.
Kevin: check torch.cuda.memory_reserved vs memory_allocated. If reserved grows but allocated doesn't, that's reserve/fragmentation.
Maria: reserved ~14G, allocated ~9G; nvidia-smi shows fragment-like allocations. also rare cudaFree errors logged when eviction fires.
sre-bot: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/runtime/gpu-mem?panel=kv-evictions  spikes line up with large batch windows.
Diana: quick experiments to validate:
  1) disable dynamic batching: BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=1
  2) enable workspace compaction on evict: REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_COMPACT=1
Maria: ran #1, memory growth stops. #2 did a vacuum pass and freed ~700MB but compaction is expensive.
Kevin: probable root causes: (1) kernel diversity causing incompatible workspace footprints, (2) dynamic batching leading to transient large allocations, (3) KV cache pins leaving mid-size free blocks.
Diana: mitigation suggestions:
- add kernel-family tag to workspace slabs so reuse tries same-family first
- tighten KV pinning/TTL for long sessions
- periodic/threshold-triggered background compaction
Kevin: I'll PR allocator metrics (per-class freelist sizes) and compaction hook. Maria, can you upload repro traces (nvprof, jemalloc dumps, pytorch trace) to the incident artifacts and link them here?
Maria: uploading now, will paste links in 10m. Thanks team.
infra-bot: CI finished: eng-runtime/gpu-mem-repro#789  compact run reduced steady-state by 620MB. artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/789
Maria: I'll write a short follow-up doc with the reproducer, traces, and suggested runtime flags tomorrow. :thumbsup:
